initiative.title: Bring tsx-data-flow into srcly
initiative.summary: One engine (tsx-data-flow analysis moved into engine/, one lazy Node child) feeds three srcly surfaces: route -> terminal graph in the dependency viewer (headline), value-path ledger from graph destinations or code-viewer expressions (PR #102), and a function-effects panel (PR #103); findings/metrics/markers/reports follow. detailed-plan.md adds the file-level design, contracts, two-tier engine session, view-state registry and the corrections a code review of both repositories forced.
initiative.next_action: User approval to start M1 (three PRs). D1-D8 defaults accepted 2026-10-23; PR #101 stays docs only.

sources.anchor: product priority order; code map primary surface
Views table; Explore it in the browser
Findings row; Metrics end-to-end; Code viewer; Graph views
route -> terminal graph is the real want, 2026-10-23
run route-graph and ledger proofs in parallel; write plan

claims.statement: srcly is the home and base layer; tsx-data-flow features merge into it.
srcly's speed must be preserved; data flow never delays the base render.
Value order (revised): route -> terminal data-flow graph in the dependency viewer first; findings/metrics/markers/reports support it.
Analysis correctness (compiler-backed identity, strict tsconfig) outranks everything else in tsx-data-flow.
Markdown output exists for agent handoff: dense, grounded, concise next action.
tsx-data-flow's own overview/report pages are transitional and need not survive.
Several Pro threads will detail branches and update this map.
Single repository: engine moves into srcly (workspace/monorepo layout only if needed).
tsx-dataflow-serve UI goes away; focus on best versions of features in srcly.
Distribution delegated to agent: choose most robust. Chosen: esbuild bundle in the wheel, system node>=18, project typescript with bundled fallback, N/A without node.
The real want is the route -> terminal data viz (Route Totality) shown in srcly dependency viewer.
All tsx-data-flow type checking and analysis logic is to be maintained.
srcly has better visuals and selection and should own the graph experience.
Value investigation: exact expression -> ordered evidence ledger + inspector, with Return/Back restoring overview.
Function effects panel in code viewer: effects, ambient reads, writes, async handling, unknowns with witnesses; no purity score.
Connectivity, coverage and value properties are separate; Not analyzed != 0; evidence bound to Program text/config/generation.
Invocation identity must be preserved; shared helper calls never join.
Never relabel import or folder edges as data flow or execution.
Existing route canvas has empty evidence-node/edge arrays; it cannot show operation order, so ordered paths use a ledger.

themes: evidence from engine, picture from srcly

conflicts.statement: tsx-data-flow says the code map is its primary surface; srcly's primary surface is the map/treemap with a modal code viewer.
conflicts.resolution: srcly's treemap stays primary; the code viewer absorbs code-map overlays (path on source, markers, where-used).

conflicts.statement: PR102 says do not merge the repositories and use a prepared external checkout (--value-analyzer).
conflicts.resolution: User decision (single repo) wins; the prepared-checkout idea survives as dev mode running engine/ from the srcly checkout.

conflicts.statement: PR102 REC-017 avoids a semantic graph on the repository map and keeps the component canvas separate; user wants the route graph in the dependency viewer.
conflicts.resolution: Data-flow mode uses its own contract in the same canvas, never overlaid on import edges; ordered path detail lives in the ledger.

conflicts.statement: PR102 wants one resident lazy Node child; PR103 starts with a one-shot JSON command and defers a resident service.
conflicts.resolution: Shape adopts one lazy child shared by all query families (Program built once); keep a one-shot command for headless report/tests; confirm with measured cold cost.

shape.appetite: Program delivered as independently revertible slices, one srcly home per slice.
shape.problem: Two tools with overlapping shells; srcly is fast but tree-sitter-only, tsx-data-flow is deep but slow and has its own UI.
shape.recommended_shape: Engine supplies evidence, srcly supplies the picture: engine (in engine/, bundled in wheel) emits a data-flow graph in srcly contract style (route -> occurrence -> step hierarchy + typed proven edges); srcly's dependency view renders it in a Data flow mode with its canvas, focus, expand-in-place, hover, keyboard and code opening. Findings/metrics/markers/reports flow through existing srcly pipelines.

success_moves: Emit route evidence in srcly's graph-contract style (hierarchy + typed proven edges) in its own Data flow mode, never on import edges.
Explain paths once: graph destinations and code-viewer expressions both open the same ordered ledger.
One lazy Node child owns one Program for all query families; base scan never waits on it.
Bind evidence to Program text, tsconfig and generation; name not-analyzed, partial, stale and budget states.
Prove each family on real anchors (solid-route; HotSpotItem.tsx:135 and HotSpotList.tsx:88/109; extractFilePath/rankHotSpots/startScan) before growing UI.
Coordinate deps layout changes with dependency-graph-legibility.

first_proof.question: Can srcly present one route's field reach in its dependency canvas and one exact value path as an ordered ledger, both from compiler-backed evidence?
first_proof.artifact: examples/solid-route rendered in the current deps canvas; HotSpotItem.tsx:135 props.node.name ledger from the code viewer.
first_proof.decision_rule: Graph: extend packing if legible, else add one route layout rule. Ledger: if generic evidence cannot prove the JSX slot exactly (and keep line 134 distinct, rank default preserving zero), fix the engine before UI.

rabbit_holes: Embedding tsx-data-flow's SPA or route-totality graph wholesale.
200K-LOC repos: engine takes ~120s; needs scoping (changed files, per-package) or a skip rule.
Monorepos with many tsconfigs: bound projects like MAX_TSC_PROJECTS.
Wheel size from bundled TypeScript fallback; measure in first proof.
Porting tsx-data-flow's graph layout/camera instead of using srcly's.
Fields with dozens of destinations rendered as a wall instead of grouped broad-use.
Merging separate helper invocations (HotSpotList row helper, line 88 vs 109).
Treating effects as a numeric risk metric.
